name: Sharmishtha
role: Daitya princess, friend of Devayani, second wife of Yayati
summary: Sharmishtha is the daughter of the daitya king Vrishaparvan. In the Mahabharata she quarrels with her friend Devayani, then serves her to protect her family, and later becomes the mother of Puru, an ancestor of the Kurus.
about: In the Mahabharata, as told by Vaishampayana in the Adi Parva, Sharmishtha is the daughter of Vrishaparvan, a king of the daityas, a class of asuras. Her father takes advice from the teacher Shukra, whose daughter Devayani is her close friend. A quarrel at a forest pool leaves Devayani in a well, and Devayani insists she will not return to the capital until Sharmishtha serves her. The text says Sharmishtha accepts, giving up her royal rank so that her father's kingdom is not left without Shukra's help. Later she asks Yayati, Devayani's husband, to father her children. Many tellings give her three sons, Druhyu, Anudruhyu (called Anu in some texts) and Puru. Puru becomes Yayati's heir, and his line, the Pauravas, leads to the Kurus. This makes Sharmishtha an ancestor of both the Pandavas and the Kauravas. The Matsya Purana also tells of her. She is still a favourite subject for writers, notably in V. S. Khandekar's Marathi novel Yayati, where she narrates part of the story herself.
kidSummary: Sharmishtha was a princess of the asuras and a friend of Devayani. After a quarrel at a forest pool, she became Devayani's maid to help her father and her kingdom. Later she became the mother of Puru, and his family tree leads to the heroes of the Mahabharata.

story.title: Two friends by a pool
story.text: Sharmishtha, a princess, and Devayani, the daughter of a famous teacher, went to bathe in a forest pool. They left their clothes on the bank.

story.title: A mix-up
story.text: In the Mahabharata, Indra became a breeze and mixed up the clothes. Each girl put on the other's, and an angry argument began.

story.title: Choosing to serve
story.text: Devayani said she would not go home until Sharmishtha served her. To keep her father's kingdom safe, Sharmishtha gave up her place as a princess and became Devayani's maid.

story.title: Her sons
story.text: Later she and King Yayati, Devayani's husband, had three sons: Druhyu, Anudruhyu and Puru. When Devayani found out, she went to her father in tears.

story.title: Puru's family
story.text: When Yayati became old suddenly, Puru agreed to take his father's old age. He became the next king, and his family later led to the Kuru kings.

teaches: Putting family and kingdom before pride
Duty and choice are not always easy to balance

family.relation: Friend, later the one she served
family.name: Devayani

places: Capital of the daitya king Vrishaparvan
Ashokavanika, an artificial Ashoka wood near her mansion

facts.text: Called to serve, Sharmishtha rode out in a palanquin with a thousand maids and told Devayani she would be her waiting-maid, following wherever Shukra gave her away.
In the Bhagavata Purana's telling, the girls rush out of their pool when Shiva passes by with his wife. In the hurry, Sharmishtha puts on Devayani's dress without knowing, and the quarrel begins.
In the Mahabharata, Sharmishtha first took Devayani's clothes by mistake, since Indra, as wind, had jumbled the heap. Only afterwards did the insults start.

Sharmishtha answered Devayani with an insult: Shukra sat lower than her father and praised him like a hired singer. She added that she could harm Devayani but not the other way round, then pushed her into a dry well.
Told that Shukra might leave the asuras unless she served Devayani, Sharmishtha agreed at once. She said the teacher and his daughter must not leave her people because of her.
After pushing Devayani into the dry well, Sharmishtha believed her friend was dead and walked home still angry. Yayati, out hunting and thirsty, arrived soon after.
Devayani would not accept a mere promise from Sharmishtha's father. She said that if Shukra truly ruled over the asura wealth, the king himself must come to her and say so.
In the Bhagavata Purana, Vrishaparvan guessed Shukra was coming to curse him. He rushed out and lay at his teacher's feet in the street before Shukra reached the house.
Shukra's condition for the marriage was plain: Yayati must never call Sharmishtha to his bed. Yayati quotes it back to her when she asks, and the curse that follows turns on that promise.
Devayani found out when three boys playing in a park pointed to Yayati as their father and named Sharmishtha as their mother. He dared not caress them, and they ran weeping to her.
To stop Shukra leaving, Sharmishtha's father said all asura treasure was his: elephants, cows, horses, even Vrishaparvan himself. Shukra replied that the way to keep him was to please Devayani.
At first Sharmishtha told Devayani that her son's father was a sage as radiant as the sun. Devayani said that if so, she had no cause for anger.
Yayati was cursed by Shukra for acting without waiting for his command. Yayati replied that refusing a woman's plea would have been a sin too, but Shukra called his act a kind of theft.
Shukra set terms: the son who gives Yayati his youth would be heir, long-lived, famous and rich in children. This is how Sharmishtha's youngest son stepped ahead of his older half-brothers.
The Bhagavata Purana derives the Usinara, Sibi, Madra and Kekaya peoples from her son Anudruhyu.
When Yayati chose her youngest son Puru as heir, townspeople said elder Yadu, Shukra's grandson, should rule. Yayati answered that the obedient son is the best son, and they agreed.
In the Bhagavata Purana, Puru answers his father's request by asking who in the world can ever repay what he owes his father. He then gladly takes the old age and gives his youth.
Puru's answer to his father was to wear the old age and give away his youth. Yayati blessed him: everyone in Puru's kingdom would have their wishes fulfilled.
In the Mahabharata, Puru's wife is Paushti. They have three heroic sons, Pravira, Ishvara and Raudrashva, and Pravira inherits the throne, followed by Manasyu.
The story is told to King Janamejaya, who is himself a Paurava. The narrator says the Pauravas descend from Puru, so Sharmishtha is an ancestor of the very king who is listening.
Tripura tradition holds that Druhyu, Sharmishtha's eldest son, founded the line that grew into the Twipra kingdom, so her sons are tied to places far from the Gangetic plain.

quiz.why: Vrishaparvan was a daitya king; Shukra was his adviser.

quiz.q: Which friend of Sharmishtha ended up in a well after their quarrel?
quiz.why: Devayani, Shukra's daughter, was left in a dry well.

quiz.q: Which son of Sharmishtha became Yayati's heir?
quiz.why: Puru agreed to take his father's old age and became the next king.

quiz.q: Sharmishtha is an ancestor of which two famous families?
quiz.why: Puru's line, the Pauravas, leads to the Kurus.

quiz.q: How many maids came with Sharmishtha when she agreed to serve Devayani?
quiz.why: She arrived in a palanquin with a thousand maids, vowing to follow wherever Devayani went.
